# WIM UI — LLM guide (llms.txt)

> Machine-readable map of the wimui React component library for coding agents. Read this before generating any UI with wimui: it defines the required CSS/setup, the correct import paths, the full component list, and the composition rules that keep screens from looking AI-generated.

## What this is

**wimui** v0.90.1 — a React 19 component library: 235 documented components across 10 categories, with design tokens, dark mode, i18n (en/ja/pt-BR) and WAI-ARIA compliant a11y. Peer deps: react ^19, react-dom ^19 (plus optional peers for specific components — see package.json).

## Install & required setup

```bash
npm i wimui
```

```ts
// 1. CSS contract — styles.css is REQUIRED (design tokens + component styles).
import "wimui/styles.css";
import "wimui/reset.css"; // optional base reset

// 2. Components — import from the root barrel or a category subpath (tree-shakeable).
import { Button, Card } from "wimui";
import { Stack, Grid } from "wimui/layout";
```

- **Theme**: wrap the app in `WimProvider` (recommended) or set `data-theme="light|dark"` on `<html>` (omit to follow OS).
- **Density**: `data-density="comfortable|compact"`, or `WimProvider` / `setWimDensity()`.
- **Never hardcode** colors / spacing / sizes in consumer code — use the `--wim-*` CSS custom properties (tokens) that styles.css defines.
- **Form + RHF** helpers live in `wimui/rhf` (react-hook-form + zod), not the root barrel.
- **Fonts are NOT bundled** and styles.css requests none. The tokens name `"Noto Sans"` (default/en/pt), `"Noto Sans JP"` (ja) and `"Noto Sans Mono"` (mono) first, then fall back to system faces — so omitting fonts is valid and renders fine. To match the documentation site, have the app load those families itself (weights 400/500/700), e.g. `npm i @fontsource/noto-sans @fontsource/noto-sans-mono` then `import "@fontsource/noto-sans/latin-400.css"` before styles.css. Do not invent a `wimui/fonts.css` — it does not exist. To use different fonts, override `--wim-font-family-*` instead.

## Import paths

Every component works from the root barrel `"wimui"`. For smaller bundles, import from its category subpath instead:

- `wimui/layout`
- `wimui/form`
- `wimui/feedback`
- `wimui/navigation`
- `wimui/data-display`
- `wimui/overlay`
- `wimui/typography`
- `wimui/media`
- `wimui/charts`
- `wimui/ai`

## Composition rules — build screens that don't look AI-generated

Single components are judged by state/a11y/token compliance. **Composed screens** are judged by hierarchy, rhythm, asymmetry and real-feeling content. Apply these whenever combining components into a screen, page, pattern or demo — **and also when you write a single component on its own**, because the way it renders with no props is judged by the same rules (rule 22). That split is about what is being judged, not about where the problem lives: a default that emits a banned pattern emits it into every screen that uses the component.

**Before laying out**: pick exactly ONE visual protagonist for the screen. If every element has the same volume, it reads as AI-generated.

**Banned patterns (the "AI signature" — do not emit):**
- `linear-gradient(135deg, …)` hero backgrounds → use surface-hierarchy tokens (`surface` / `surface-raised`) to separate planes.
- The stock hero (badge → big heading → subtext → two solid/outline buttons) → asymmetric composition led by one protagonist.
- "Rule of three" equal feature cards (icon + short heading + one line, ×3) → let the count follow content (2 or 5 is fine); vary card size and copy length.
- Emoji used as UI icons (☰ ★ ✓) → use `src/icon/` components. (Emoji as functional markers in docs/README is fine; as UI icons it is not.)
- Skeleton used as anything but loading (fake screenshots) → real-looking content or an actual mini UI.
- Every section center-aligned → default to left-aligned; at most one centered section per page.
- Round numbers ("1000+", "99%") + generic copy ("Get started") → jagged realistic numbers (4,281) and product-specific voice.
- Sequential/alphabetical dummy names (Alice/Bob/Charlie, User 1/2) → culturally diverse, unordered, real-feeling names.
- Rainbow color-per-category → color carries state only (success/warning/danger); everything else neutral.
- Perfectly even grids (2×2, 3×3 all same size) → break the grid (span the protagonist cell, size differences, hero+sidebar asymmetry).
- Filling every slot / uniform gaps everywhere → leave whitespace; group by proximity (tight within a group, loose between groups).

**Machine-enforced banned vocabulary** (a linter, `check:slop`, fails builds that use these in demo copy — say concrete actions/numbers instead):
- Hype adjectives/verbs: seamless, powerful, effortless, cutting-edge, next-gen, next-generation, revolutionary, game-changing, state-of-the-art, world-class, best-in-class, unparalleled, lightning-fast, blazing-fast, supercharge, innovative, disruptive, harness, leverage, elevate, empower, reimagine, unleash, delight, magical, 圧倒的, 革新的, 次世代, 究極, 最先端.
- Hype phrases: "in today's digital landscape", "built for the modern team", "supercharge your", "unleash your", "reimagine the way", "experience the power of", "innovative solutions".
- Stock placeholder names: John Doe, Jane Doe, John Smith, Jane Smith, Lorem Ipsum, Example User, Acme, Alice, Bob, Charlie, User 1, User 2, User 3, Step 1, Step 2, Step 3 (a realistic example name in an input placeholder is fine).

**Must rules:**
1. One visual protagonist per screen (jump in size/weight/color creates the entry point).
2. Contrast density: hero/showcase sparse, data regions (tables/lists) dense. Uniform "medium density" reads as AI.
3. Never override a component's defaults via inline `style` (`padding:0`, `borderRadius:0`). Add a prop/token instead.
4. Never hardcode gap/padding/size — use `--wim-spacing-*` tokens.
5. Keep one radius stance per screen (`radius.component` / `radius.container` / `radius.overlay`); don't mix 0 and lg arbitrarily. Narrow table cards must share the same radius token as the adjacent toolbar/pagination chrome — not jump to `radius.container` while chrome stays on `radius.component`.
6. Limit accent color: primary surfaces (solid buttons, emphasis backgrounds) 1–2 per view.
7. Give demo content real substance (product-context copy, internally consistent numbers/dates/names — active ≤ total, dates not evenly spaced).
8. Build realism inside a world the reader already knows. Chasing substance pushes toward niche expertise, and a screen set in one (a shipyard's watch orders, a trading desk, a clinical protocol) makes the reader decode the domain before they can see the components — the pattern stops teaching. Pick an everyday situation (renting a car and returning it, a delivery, a hospital appointment) and keep specialist vocabulary out of the places that carry state and actions. The test: can a reader say what the screen is for without a paragraph of explanation?
9. Never show the result of an action the screen cannot perform. Coverage-driven composition puts the component first and invents a state that justifies it, so the reader sees outcomes ("not in the record", "1 photo") with no control that could have produced them. Reachable state is (1) what the controls on this screen can do, and (2) values the subject already holds. Use the component inside a reachable moment; don't invent an unreachable one to justify the component. The test: can you arrive at what is on screen using only the controls that are on screen?
10. Keep one elevation stance per screen: don't mix surfaces raised by shadow with surfaces cut by borders. `Card` and `Stats` default to `elevated`, so pass `variant="outline"` when the screen is border-led. If the outer container already casts a shadow, its contents need only a border. On admin/list screens, `Table`/`DataGrid` mobile cards must stay border-only like the toolbar and pagination — row cards with `shadow-sm` while chrome is flat outline is the same mixed stance.
11. Never wrap a component that already draws its own frame. `<Card><Table card /></Card>` doubles the border and nests radii (12px inside 4px). `Table` takes a `card` prop and `Stats` is already a Card — place them directly.
12. Always pass `intent` on `Badge` / `Tag` / `Chip`. Their default is `primary` (the accent), so an ordinary value like `pending` or `member` gets painted as loudly as an exception and the colour stops carrying information. Use `intent="neutral"` for ordinary values.
13. Pick colour by good/bad, not by direction. On `Stats.Trend`, `direction` sets the arrow and `intent` sets the colour; without `intent` the colour follows the direction, so `up` is the success colour. For a metric where up is bad (failures, error rate, cost), write `direction="up" intent="danger"` — leaving it out renders the bad news as good. Don't approximate a meaning the API cannot express.
14. Keep the chrome quiet. Breadcrumb, page title, summary line, toolbar and filter bar frame the content; they must not compete with the protagonist. Don't promote a one-line summary to an `Alert`/`Banner`, don't wrap the filter bar in a `Card` (its border doubles up with the data region's), keep primary surfaces out of the chrome, and don't stack a KPI tile row above a table screen. Corollary of protagonist and accent limits, but it is the rule most often broken on admin/list screens — the test is whether the eye lands on the data first.
15. Add intentional "wobble": mix in 1–2 incomplete rows (a truncated long name, a missing optional field, an extreme value, an error/unread state) and show non-happy-path states (hover/focus/disabled/error/empty/loading).
16. Check the screen at 390px and 768px before calling it done. The page itself must never scroll sideways (`document.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth` is a bug — the usual cause is a group of controls that cannot wrap, e.g. several buttons packed into one `Toolbar.Group`; split them into separate groups). Data tables need their narrow mode turned on (`<DataGrid mobileCard>` / `<Table mobileCard>`) rather than an inner scrollbar: without it columns collapse and a short string like a `Code` lot number breaks one character per line. The default card switch is `container-down(sm)` (576px). Wide grids that still overflow at tablet should pass `mobileCard="md"` so cards continue through 768px.
17. Left-align by default. At most one centred section per page, counted per section — cards repeated inside one grid count as one, and this exemption is about how to count centring only: the repetition of a uniform grid is still caught by the rule-of-three rule.
18. Never fall back to three equal parallel items (three feature cards with icon + short heading + one line, or "Fast. Secure. Reliable."). Let the count come from the content — two or five is fine — and vary card grain and body length.
19. Subtract every decoration that does not help the reader act or understand (excess shadow, border, gradient, emoji). AI fills empty space by habit, so decoration accumulates without intent.
20. Never hand-draw fake chrome (browser bars, phone frames, IDE windows) to make a demo look like a screenshot.
21. Never fall back to a stock diagonal gradient (a 135deg hero background, a `to bottom right` panel, a gradient blob). Split surfaces with the surface tokens instead. Gradients parallel to an axis are fine when they implement motion (a 90deg shimmer).
22. Judge a component the way it renders with no props. If placing it bare produces something on the banned list — a stock hero, three equal feature cards, a diagonal gradient panel, rainbow categories, empty placeholder copy — the default is the defect, not the screen that used it. Catalogue "Default" stories teach the component, so they are read as composition, not as craft.
23. Never ship hollow boilerplate copy ("No data found", "Get started", "This is a description", "Ready to start?", "Your operation has been executed"). It displays the fact that nobody decided what to say yet. Name the thing that is missing and the one action that changes it. This is a different defect from hype: hype overclaims, hollow copy says nothing.
24. Avoid the stock hero anatomy: icon or badge, big heading, one line of subtext, two buttons (one solid, one outline), all centred. It is the single most recognisable AI screen. Decide one protagonist and build asymmetrically around it; one primary action plus a text link beats two equal buttons.
25. Never assign a different colour per tag, per person or per KPI. Colour carries good/bad (success / warning / danger) and nothing else; everything else stays neutral. A rainbow of categories makes every value look like an exception, which means none of them do.
26. Never draw a stand-in for content you did not build: a Skeleton used as a fake screenshot, a grey box or gradient panel captioned "Chart placeholder". Either put the real component in (a Sparkline, a table) or leave the region out. A labelled empty box teaches readers that the library cannot fill it.
27. Glass / neumorphic "futuristic tech" surfaces may exist as an opt-in variant, but never as a default or as the first example in the docs. Shown first, it becomes what the library looks like, and that look is the most generic one available.
28. Put the hamburger on the side the menu comes from: top-left for a drawer that slides in from the left (AppShell with Sidebar), the end of the bar for a full menu that drops from the top (Navbar.Menu). Keep it uncovered while the menu is open, because it turns into the close button; do not dim the header with the overlay so that tapping the overlay is the only way out. Use one pattern per app, so the trigger does not jump sides between screens.

## Recipes — copy-paste starting points

### 1. Required setup (the contract)

Without `styles.css` nothing is styled — this is the one step Storybook hides from you. Import it once at the app entry, wrap the tree in `WimProvider`, then build screens inside.

```tsx
// main.tsx — app entry
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import "wimui/styles.css"; // REQUIRED: design tokens + component styles
import "wimui/reset.css";  // optional base reset
import { WimProvider } from "wimui";
import { App } from "./App";

// theme: "light" | "dark" | "system" (default). density: "comfortable" | "compact".
createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <WimProvider theme="system" density="comfortable">
    <App />
  </WimProvider>,
);
```

```tsx
// App.tsx — app frame. AppShell wires header/sidebar; page content is children.
import { AppShell, Header, Sidebar, Stack, Title, Text, Button } from "wimui";

export function App() {
  return (
    <AppShell
      header={<Header sticky bordered><Title tag="h1" size="md">Larkfield</Title></Header>}
      sidebar={
        <Sidebar width={240}>
          <Stack gap="2xs" p="md">
            <Button variant="ghost" justify="start" fullWidth>Overview</Button>
            <Button variant="ghost" justify="start" fullWidth>Customers</Button>
            <Button variant="ghost" justify="start" fullWidth>Settings</Button>
          </Stack>
        </Sidebar>
      }
    >
      <Stack gap="lg">
        <Title tag="h2" size="lg">Overview</Title>
        <Text color="secondary">Spacing/size/color come from --wim-* tokens via props — never hardcode px/hex.</Text>
      </Stack>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

### 2. A composed content screen

One protagonist (the KPI row), a dense table below, tokens via props, jagged real data, and one deliberately incomplete row. Note the compound components (`Stats.Value`, `Table.Head`) and that `Grid` uses `cols` (not `columns`).

```tsx
import { Stack, Grid, Card, Stats, Table, Badge, Title, Text } from "wimui";

const rows = [
  { id: "in_9f2a", name: "Marisol Okonkwo", plan: "Scale", amount: "$4,610.50", status: "paid" },
  { id: "in_7b41", name: "Dmitri Sørensen", plan: "Enterprise", amount: "$12,199.00", status: "failed" },
  { id: "in_2a90", name: "Thomas O'Reilly", plan: null, amount: "$89.00", status: "pending" }, // incomplete row
] as const;
const intent = { paid: "success", failed: "danger", pending: undefined } as const;

export function BillingOverview() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <Title tag="h2" size="lg">Billing</Title>

      {/* Protagonist: KPI row. Uneven content per tile — not three clones. */}
      <Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }} gap="md">
        <Stats><Stats.Label>MRR</Stats.Label><Stats.Value>$48,210</Stats.Value><Stats.Trend>+6.4%</Stats.Trend></Stats>
        <Stats><Stats.Label>Active workspaces</Stats.Label><Stats.Value>1,204</Stats.Value><Stats.Description>176 idle over 30 days</Stats.Description></Stats>
        <Stats><Stats.Label>Failed webhooks</Stats.Label><Stats.Value>137</Stats.Value><Stats.Trend>+23 today</Stats.Trend></Stats>
      </Grid>

      {/* Dense data region */}
      <Card padding="none">
        <Table hoverable fullWidth>
          <Table.Header>
            <Table.Row>
              <Table.Head>Customer</Table.Head><Table.Head>Plan</Table.Head>
              <Table.Head>Amount</Table.Head><Table.Head>Status</Table.Head>
            </Table.Row>
          </Table.Header>
          <Table.Body>
            {rows.map((r) => (
              <Table.Row key={r.id}>
                <Table.Cell>{r.name}</Table.Cell>
                <Table.Cell>{r.plan ?? <Text color="tertiary">—</Text>}</Table.Cell>
                <Table.Cell>{r.amount}</Table.Cell>
                <Table.Cell><Badge variant="subtle" intent={intent[r.status]}>{r.status}</Badge></Table.Cell>
              </Table.Row>
            ))}
          </Table.Body>
        </Table>
      </Card>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

> More verified full-screen recipes (auth sign-in, settings form, empty state, filtered data table, onboarding) and per-category idioms (form, navigation, feedback, overlay) are in `llms-full.txt`.
## Components

### layout — `import { … } from "wimui/layout"`

- **AppShell** — Basic application shell layout (aka UI Shell, Page Layout, Split Page Layout)
- **AspectRatio** — Fixed ratio container
- **BentoGrid** — Modern card grid (aka Waffle Menu, Bento Menu, Grid Menu, Candy Bar Menu, Chocolate Bar Menu, ベントーメニュー, ワッフルメニュー)
- **Box** — Polymorphic box
- **Center** — Radial centering
- **Container** — Layout wrapper
- **Dashboard** — Arranges widgets in a configurable grid with an edit mode for adding, removing, and resizing them.
- **Divider** — Content separator (aka Separator, Horizontal Rule)
- **Flex** — Flexible layout
- **Footer** — Lower navigation
- **Grid** — Flexbox or CSS Grid system (aka Layout Grid)
- **Group** — Flexible grouping (aka Wrap, Inline Stack, Space, Inline)
- **Header** — Upper navigation (aka Top Bar, App Bar)
- **InteractiveArea** — Foundation component for consistent interactive areas with borders and states.
- **Masonry** — Waterfall grid
- **Navbar** — Primary navigation
- **OverflowList** — Lays out items in one row and folds the ones that do not fit into a "+N" indicator. (aka Overflow, Overflow Handler)
- **PageHeader** — Head of a page: breadcrumb, title (always h1), status, description, actions and tabs in a fixed order and spacing. (aka Pagehead)
- **ScrollArea** — A custom scrollbar component that provides high-performance, cross-browser consistent themes while maintaining a native-like feel. (aka Scroll Panel, Scrollable Region)
- **Sidebar** — A collapsible navigation or informational panel on the side of the screen (aka Source List, Inspector, Nav Drawer, Side Nav, Side Navigation)
- **SimpleGrid** — Responsive fixed grid (aka Inline Grid)
- **Splitter** — Split and resize panels (aka Resizable, Resizable Panels, Split Pane, Resizer, Resize Box)
- **Stack** — Vertical/Horizontal alignment (aka Block Stack)
- **Toolbar** — Action strip for IconButton, ToggleGroup, and related controls with toolbar keyboard navigation. (aka Action Bar)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In React Spectrum 2, "ActionBar" is the bar of bulk actions that appears while items are selected — that is `SelectionBar` here. WIM's `Toolbar` is a persistent row of controls.
- **Transition** — Utilities for managing smooth enter and leave animations with CSS classes
- **VisuallyHidden** — Hide content visually while keeping it accessible to screen readers (aka Screen Reader Only, SR Only)
- **Watermark** — Translucent text or images overlaid on content to indicate ownership or status

### form — `import { … } from "wimui/form"`

- **Button** — Action triggers
- **ButtonGroup** — Group of buttons (aka Button Set, Action Set, Action Button Group)
- **Cascader** — Hierarchical selection (aka Column View, Miller Columns, Cascade Select)
- **Checkbox** — Multiple choice
- **CheckboxGroup** — Shared state checkboxes
- **ColorInput** — Input with color preview (aka Color Well, Color Field)
- **ColorPicker** — Color selection picker (aka Swatch Picker, Color Swatch Picker)
- **Combobox** — Select with search (aka Autocomplete, Auto Complete, Suggest)
- **CopyButton** — Copy to clipboard (aka Copy, Clipboard)
- **CounterTextarea** — Textarea with character count display
- **CreditCardInput** — Payment card input with brand detection
- **DatePicker** — Date selection (aka Date Input, Date Field)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In Blueprint, a "DatePicker" is the calendar panel shown inline — that is `Calendar` here. WIM's `DatePicker` is a text field that opens a calendar, which Blueprint calls DateInput.
- **DateRangePicker** — Date range selection (aka Date Range Input)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In Blueprint, a "DateRangePicker" is the calendar panel for choosing a range — that is `RangeCalendar` here. WIM's `DateRangePicker` is a pair of date fields, which Blueprint calls DateRangeInput.
- **Dropzone** — Drag & drop files
- **FieldError** — Validation messages (aka Inline Error, Error Message)
- **Fieldset** — Form grouping (aka Form Group)
- **FieldTemplate** — Standardizes label placement, required markings, and error message display for all form-related components. (aka Field, Form Control)
- **FileUpload** — File selection (aka Upload, File Input, File Uploader, File Trigger)
- **FloatButton** — Floating action buttons (aka FAB)
- **IconButton** — A square button containing only an icon without a text label. (aka Close Button)
- **ImageCropper** — Front-end image cropping and rotation tool. (aka Cropper)
- **InlineEdit** — A component that allows users to switch between a view-only mode and an editable mode in-place. (aka Editable Text, Edit In Place, Editable, Inplace)
- **Input** — Single-line input fields for text, numbers, or emails (aka Text Input, Text Field, Input Text)
- **InputBase** — Standardizes the visual container, icon slots (Prefix/Suffix), and clear button behavior for text-based inputs.
- **InputGroup** — Inputs with icons/labels (aka Control Group)
- **InputMask** — Formatted inputs (aka Masked Input)
- **LinkButton** — Anchor styled as button (aka Anchor Button)
- **Mentions** — @ / # suggestions (aka Mention)
- **MultiSelect** — Multiple selection (aka Tag Picker, Select Panel, Select Multiple)
- **NumberInput** — Input with step adjustments (aka Spin Button, Numeric Stepper, Numeric Input, Number Field, Input Number)
- **OtpInput** — One-time password fields (aka Pin Input, Input OTP, PIN Code Input, One Time Password Field, OTP Field, Pin Code, Verification Code)
- **PasswordInput** — Password with toggle (aka Password Toggle Field)
- **PasswordStrength** — Visual meter to indicate password security level. (aka Strength Meter)
- **PhoneInput** — International phone number input
- **QueryBuilder** — Visual builder for constructing complex search queries. (aka Condition Builder)
- **Radio** — Single choice (aka Radio Button)
- **RadioGroup** — Shared state radio buttons (aka Radio Button Group, Choice List)
- **RangeSlider** — Range selection (aka Range Selector)
- **Rating** — Star rating (aka Star Rating, Rating Indicator, Rating Display, Rating Group, Rate)
- **RichTextEditor** — WYSIWYG rich text editor (aka Editor)
- **SearchInput** — Search with clear button (aka Search Field, Search Bar, Search Box)
- **SegmentedControl** — Button-style controls for switching between a small set of mutually exclusive options (aka Segmented Buttons, Segmented Picker, Content Switcher, Segment Group, Select Button)
- **Select** — A dropdown menu for selecting one option from a predefined list (aka Pop-Up Button, Select Menu, Picker)
- **SignaturePad** — Handwritten signature input
- **Slider** — An input to capture a numeric value from a specified range by dragging a knob (aka Range, Range Input)
- **SmartSearchInput** — Smart search input enabling both traditional search and AI prompting.
- **SplitButton** — SplitButton description. (aka Combo Button)
- **Switch** — A binary switch for instantly toggling settings between on and off states (aka Toggle, Toggle Switch, Input Switch)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In Radix, shadcn/ui and Ark UI, a "Toggle" is a button that stays pressed (`aria-pressed`) — use a one-item `ToggleGroup` here. WIM's `Switch` is the on/off control that Apple and Material call a toggle.
- **SwitchGroup** — Shared state switches
- **TagInput** — Input field for creating free-form tags. (aka Token Field, Chips Input, Tags Input, Text Input With Tokens, Input Tag)
- **Textarea** — Multi-line input fields for longer text entries like descriptions or comments (aka Input Textarea)
- **ThemeToggle** — Light / dark / system theme switcher (aka Animated Theme Toggler)
- **TimePicker** — Time selection (aka Time Field, Time Input)
- **ToggleGroup** — Toggleable buttons (aka Toggle Button Group)
- **Transfer** — Move items between lists (aka Pick List)
- **TreeSelect** — Select from tree structure

### feedback — `import { … } from "wimui/feedback"`

- **Alert** — Important messages (aka Message Bar, Callout, Flash, Inline Alert, Inline Message, Section Message)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In Fluent UI v8, a "Callout" is a popup anchored to an element — that is `Popover` here. WIM's `Alert` matches Blueprint's Callout: an inline message in the page flow.
- **Autosave** — Inline status indicator for automatic save state
- **Banner** — Top prominent messages
- **ErrorBoundary** — Runtime error fallback
- **Indicator** — Small status dots (aka Badge Indicator, Message Indicator)
- **Loader** — Animated indicators to show that data is loading or processing
- **LoadingOverlay** — Overlay with loading indicator (aka Block UI)
- **Notification** — Rich notification card
- **Progress** — Progress bar (aka Progress Bar, Progress Linear)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: Material's "Progress Indicator" covers indeterminate spinners as well. WIM's `Progress` is determinate and linear only — for the indeterminate case use `Spinner`.
- **ProgressRing** — ProgressRing description. (aka Progress Circle, Animated Circular Progress Bar, Radial Progress, Progress Circular)
- **Result** — Task status indicator (aka Full Page Error)
- **ScrollProgress** — Reading progress indicator
- **Skeleton** — Placeholder for content loading states. (aka Shimmer, Skeleton Loader)
- **Snackbar** — Bottom notifications
- **Spinner** — A rotating icon indicating background activity or data fetching (aka Activity Indicator, Inline Loading, Loading, Progress Spinner, Spin)
- **Toast** — Non-intrusive floating messages that provide feedback on system operations (aka Message, Sonner, Toaster, Flag)
- **Tour** — Sequential guided walkthroughs to onboard users or highlight features (aka Teaching Popover, Coach Mark, User Guide, Spotlight)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In Atlassian's design system, "Spotlight" is the onboarding tour that highlights one element at a time — that is `Tour` here. Aceternity UI's Spotlight is a decorative lighting effect, which WIM does not provide.

### navigation — `import { … } from "wimui/navigation"`

- **Affix** — Sticky elements (aka Sticky)
- **Anchor** — Smooth scroll links (aka Scrollspy, Table of Contents, TableOfContents, TOC)
- **BackTop** — Back to top button (aka Back to Top, Scroll Top)
- **Breadcrumb** — Location trace (aka Path Bar, Path Control, Breadcrumbs)
- **CommandPalette** — Cmd+K search overlay (aka Command Bar, Quick Open, Omnibar, Command)
- **HamburgerMenu** — Toggleable menu (aka Sandwich Menu, Navigation Drawer Trigger, Nav Toggle, Cheeseburger Menu, Veggie Burger Menu, Pancake Menu, Bacon Menu, Hot Dog Menu, ハンバーガーメニュー, サンドイッチメニュー, Hamburger)
- **KeyboardShortcuts** — Display a structured list of keyboard shortcuts (aka Hotkeys)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: Blueprint's Hotkeys also registers the key bindings. WIM's `KeyboardShortcuts` only shows the list of shortcuts; bind the keys in your app.
- **Link** — Hyperlinks
- **Menubar** — Desktop-style application menu bar with floating File / Edit / View submenus.
- **Pagination** — Multi-page navigation (aka Pagination Nav, Paginator)
- **SkipLink** — A link at the very top of the page that jumps past the header and navigation to the main content. It stays hidden until it receives keyboard focus. AppShell renders one by default. (aka Skip Nav, Skip Navigation, Skip to Content, Bypass Block)
- **SpeedDial** — Floating action button that expands sub-actions on hover or click.
- **Stepper** — Visual sequence steps (aka Progress Indicator, Steps, Wizard, Progress Tracker)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In Apple HIG and macOS, a "Stepper" is the control that increments a number — that is `NumberInput` here. WIM's `Stepper` shows progress through a sequence of steps, which is what Material calls a Stepper.
- **TabBar** — Mobile bottom navigation (aka Bottom Navigation, Bottom Tab Bar)
- **TabNavigation** — Tab-based navigation (aka Tab Menu, Tab Nav, Underline Nav, Sub Nav)
- **Tabs** — A container to organize related content into switchable view panels (aka Tab List, Tab View, Tab Group)

### data-display — `import { … } from "wimui/data-display"`

- **Accordion** — Collapsible panels (aka Disclosure, Disclosure Group, Expander, Collapse, Expansion Panel)
- **Avatar** — Profile initials/pics (aka User Avatar)
- **AvatarGroup** — Stacked avatars (aka Face Pile, Avatar Circles, Avatar Stack)
- **Badge** — Indicators or counts (aka Icon Indicator, State Label, Lozenge)
- **Barcode** — Draws a scannable Code 128 or EAN-13 barcode.
- **Calendar** — Calendar view
- **CalendarHeatmap** — GitHub-style activity graph for visualizing continuity
- **Card** — Information containers (aka Tile)
- **Carousel** — Content slideshow
- **Chip** — Filter/Selection tokens (aka Pill, Token)
- **Comment** — Shows one comment in a discussion, with its actions and nested replies.
- **Countdown** — Display the remaining time until a target moment as a live ticking timer, for sale deadlines, OTP resend waits, and maintenance notices. (aka Timer)
- **DataGrid** — Advanced data table and manipulation (aka Data Table, Index Table, Table View, Dynamic Table)
- **DescriptionList** — Key-value pairs (aka Data List, Labeled Value, Descriptions, Name Value List)
- **EmptyState** — Missing data placeholder (aka Blank Slate, Zero State, Non-Ideal State, Empty Search Result, Illustrated Message, Empty)
- **FAQSection** — Frequently Asked Questions section
- **InfiniteScroll** — Infinite scroll control (aka Data Scroller)
- **JsonDiffViewer** — Compares two JSON values as a formatted side-by-side or unified diff, built on top of CodeDiffViewer.
- **JsonViewer** — Recursive tree viewer and editor for JSON data. (aka JSON Tree View)
- **Kanban** — Drag-and-drop board for visualizing workflow stages
- **Leaderboard** — Display a ranked list of entries with scores. Medal colors for the top three are opt-in.
- **List** — Structurally organized items in bullet points or numbered formats (aka Contained List, Ordered List, Unordered List, Card List, Resource List, List View)
- **Markdown** — A component for safely rendering text in Markdown format.
- **Marquee** — Scrolling text animation (aka Ticker, Infinite Moving Cards)
- **NodeGraph** — Visualizes complex networks and relationships between nodes.
- **Persona** — Shows a person as one unit: avatar, name and up to two lines of description, with text sizes matched to the avatar. The name is read once.
- **PivotTable** — Draws aggregated data as a table with multi-level row and column headings, subtotals and grand totals. (aka Pivot, Cross Tab, Crosstab)
- **Presence** — Shows whether a person is online, away, busy, or offline.
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In Ark UI and Chakra UI, "Presence" is the helper that animates an element in and out as it mounts and unmounts — that is `Transition` here. WIM's `Presence` shows whether a person is online, away, busy or offline.
- **PullToRefresh** — Pull-to-refresh utility for enhancing mobile user experience.
- **QRCode** — QR generator
- **RangeCalendar** — Range calendar view
- **Reaction** — Display emoji reaction buttons with toggleable state and counts
- **RelativeTime** — Display a timestamp as a localized relative phrase ("3 minutes ago", "yesterday") that updates automatically as time passes.
- **ScheduleView** — Displays tasks or events on a chronological timeline or calendar view.
- **SelectionBar** — Bar above a table that shows the number of selected rows, the actions for them and a way to clear the selection. Announces the count to screen readers. (aka Bulk Actions, Batch Actions, Table Selection Toolbar, Select All Actions)
- **SortableList** — Item rearrangement and reordering (aka Order List)
- **Stats** — A component to highlight key performance indicators and metrics (aka Statistic, Stat, Big Number, Metric Text)
- **SwipeableList** — Container for SwipeAction rows that keeps at most one row open at a time. (aka Swipeable List)
- **SwipeAction** — Mobile-friendly swipe actions (delete, archive) for list items.
- **Table** — Rows and columns for displaying structured data efficiently (aka Structured List, HTML Table)
- **Tag** — Compact visual descriptors used for labeling or categorizing content (aka Interaction Tag, Topic Tag)
- **Timeline** — A vertical list mapping events or history in chronological order
- **TreeDiagram** — Lays out a tree such as an org chart from the data alone, with parents centred over their children and collapsible subtrees. (aka Org Chart, Tree Chart, Hierarchy Diagram, Organization Chart)
- **TreeView** — Hierarchical data (aka Outline View, Tree, Flat Tree, File Tree, Navigation Tree)
- **VirtualList** — Efficiently renders large lists by virtualizing off-screen items (aka Virtual Scroller, Virtualizer, Virtual Scroll)

### overlay — `import { … } from "wimui/overlay"`

- **BottomSheet** — Mobile bottom overlay (aka Sheet, Action Sheet)
- **Confirm** — Opens a confirmation dialog from code with await confirm() and returns true or false. (aka Alert Dialog, Confirmation Dialog, Confirm Dialog)
- **ContextMenu** — Right-click menus
- **Dialog** — Focused task windows (aka Modal, Modal Dialog, Composed Modal)
- **Drawer** — Slide-out detail panels (aka Navigation Drawer, Overlay Drawer, Side Panel, Side Sheet)
- **Dropdown** — Overlay selection menu (aka Overflow Menu, Kebab Menu, Meatball Menu, Vertical Ellipsis, Horizontal Ellipsis, Three Dots Menu, More Menu, App Switcher, オーバーフローメニュー, ケバブメニュー, ミートボールメニュー, Menu Button, Action Menu, Dropdown Menu)
- **FocusTrap** — Focus management (aka Trap Focus, Focus Scope)
- **HoverCard** — Rich content on hover (aka Preview Card, Preview Trigger)
- **Menu** — General menus (aka Action List, Tiered Menu, Panel Menu, Nav List)
  - ⚠️ Not the same as elsewhere: In macOS, a "Menu" is the pull-down from a menu bar. WIM's `Menu` is the list of choices itself; for one that opens from a trigger, use `Dropdown`.
- **Popconfirm** — Confirmation overlay (aka Confirm Popup)
- **Popover** — Contextual overlay (aka Info Label, Info Button, Toggletip, Overlay Panel, Contextual Help, Drop Button, Inline Dialog, Popup)
- **Portal** — Out-of-hierarchy render
- **Tooltip** — Information on hover (aka Help Tag, Tip)

### typography — `import { … } from "wimui/typography"`

- **Blockquote** — Visually separates external quotes or text to be emphasized.
- **Code** — Code snippets (aka Inline Code)
- **Highlight** — Text highlighting (aka Mark, Highlighter)
- **Kbd** — Keyboard shortcuts (aka Key Combo, Keybinding Hint, Keyboard Key, Keyboard)
- **Label** — Descriptive text for input fields, including required/optional marks
- **Legend** — Group title
- **Span** — Lightweight wrapper for inline text or short labels with icon support
- **Spoiler** — Collapse long text such as reviews and comments to a fixed number of lines, with an accessible "show more" toggle that appears only when the text overflows.
- **Text** — Has appropriate line-height and spacing to ensure readability of long text. (aka Truncated Text, Truncate, Paragraph)
- **Title** — Possesses visual weight (boldness/size) to indicate page structure. (aka Heading)

### media — `import { … } from "wimui/media"`

- **Audio** — Audio playback (aka Audio Player)
- **Gallery** — Displays a responsive image grid with configurable columns, aspect ratios, multi-select, and an optional lightbox. (aka Galleria)
- **Icon** — Visual symbols
- **Image** — Image content (aka Thumbnail)
- **ImageCompare** — ImageCompare overlays two images and reveals them with a draggable divider — a before/after slider for comparing edits, restorations, or AI-generated results against their source. (aka Compare Slider)
- **Lightbox** — A high-quality overlay component for displaying images and media with gallery and zoom functionality. (aka Image Viewer)
- **Video** — A component for embedding and controlling local or remote video content (aka Video Player)

### charts — `import { … } from "wimui/charts"`

- **AreaChart** — Area charts
- **BarChart** — Bar charts
- **BoxPlot** — Five-number summary of a distribution per group
- **CandlestickChart** — Open, high, low and close per period
- **FunnelChart** — Process stage abandonment chart
- **GanttChart** — Project schedule and timeline visualization
- **GaugeChart** — KPI goal achievement chart
- **Heatmap** — Graphical representation of data where individual values are contained in a matrix as colors.
- **LineChart** — Line charts
- **PieChart** — Proportional parts of a whole chart
- **RadarChart** — Multivariate data on concentric axes chart
- **SankeyChart** — Flow chart where band width is the amount
- **ScatterChart** — Scatter plots
- **Sparkline** — Tiny inline trend chart
- **Treemap** — Hierarchical data area-based display (aka Distribution)
- **WaterfallChart** — Running total broken into its contributions

### ai — `import { … } from "wimui/ai"`

- **AgentStatus** — Real-time agent state indicator (thinking / running / waiting)
- **AILabel** — Marks a value or a block as produced by AI. Pressing the mark opens an explanation of what the AI did.
- **AIResponseFeedback** — Thumbs-up/down feedback controls and regenerate button for AI responses. (aka Thumbs Rating)
- **ArtifactsOverlay** — ArtifactsOverlay is a specialized side-panel for displaying large AI-generated content (Artifacts) without interrupting the main chat context.
- **ChatUI** — A comprehensive set of components for building chat interfaces with support for messages, avatars, timestamps, and interactive input. (aka Chat, AI Chat Dialogue)
- **CodeBlock** — Syntax-highlighted code block with copy button, line numbers, and collapsible overflow. (aka Code Snippet, Code Highlight)
- **CodeDiffViewer** — Displays code changes as a side-by-side or unified diff, with line-level highlighting and Apply/Reject actions. (aka Code Comparison)
- **InteractiveGraph** — InteractiveGraph provides a canvas for visualizing node-based data. Ideal for RAG knowledge bases, agent workflows, or state machines.
- **MarkdownRenderer** — MarkdownRenderer converts a markdown string into WIM UI components. It uses react-markdown under the hood and applies WIM's typography system. (aka Markdown Render)
- **ModelSelector** — ModelSelector is a dropdown for switching between AI models, surfacing the metadata that matters when choosing one — context window size and per-token pricing.
- **PromptInput** — Interactive input optimized for AI prompt engineering with multi-line support and action triggers. (aka AI Chat Input)
- **SourceCitation** — Displays cited sources with title, domain, and external link for AI-generated content.
- **StreamingText** — Renders text with a typewriter-like animation, ideal for AI chat responses.
- **Terminal** — Renders terminal-style output with ANSI color support, prompt prefixes, and copy/clear controls.
- **ThoughtProcess** — Visualizes AI reasoning steps and execution states in a timeline format.
- **ThreadList** — ThreadList renders a conversation-history sidebar for AI chat apps — a scrollable list of past threads with an optional new-conversation action and per-thread deletion.
- **UsageMeter** — UsageMeter (also exported as TokenCounter) visualizes token consumption against a budget such as a model's context window — a labeled bar plus a numeric readout that shifts to warning and danger colors near the limit. (aka Level Indicator, Capacity Indicator, Meter)
- **VoiceVisualizer** — Animated voice-level indicator (bars / waveform)

## Hooks

Exported hooks. Prefer them over hand-rolled equivalents (`matchMedia` listeners, textarea height math, sort state).

- **useAnnounce** — `import { useAnnounce } from "wimui"` — Announce the result of an action to screen readers — "Saved", "3 results", "Moved to Done".
- **useAutoResize** — `import { useAutoResize } from "wimui"` — Grow a `<textarea>` with its content, up to `maxRows` rows; past that it scrolls. `Textarea` and `PromptInput` already do this — use the hook only for a textarea you render yourself.
- **useBreakpoint** — `import { useBreakpoint } from "wimui"` — Resolve the current active breakpoint — the largest whose min-width the viewport satisfies. Returns the smallest breakpoint below the first threshold. SSR-safe (defaults to the smallest until mounted).
- **useBreakpointDown** — `import { useBreakpointDown } from "wimui"` — Track whether the viewport is below a named breakpoint (max-width), mirroring the SCSS `down()` mixin — the JS equivalent of HamburgerMenu's `visibleBelow`. SSR-safe.
- **useBreakpointUp** — `import { useBreakpointUp } from "wimui"` — Track whether the viewport is at or above a named breakpoint (min-width), mirroring the SCSS `up()` mixin. SSR-safe.
- **useConfirm** — `import { useConfirm } from "wimui/overlay"` — Ask the user to confirm an action and wait for the answer, from anywhere under `ConfirmProvider`. Resolves to true when the user confirms, and to false when they cancel, press Escape, or the provider unmounts. Use it before an action the user cannot easily undo; for an action that can be undone, run it and offer Undo in a `Snackbar` instead.
- **useMediaQuery** — `import { useMediaQuery } from "wimui"` — Subscribe to a CSS media query and track whether it currently matches.
- **useNotification** — `import { useNotification } from "wimui/feedback"` — Show a notification card in a corner of the screen from anywhere under `NotificationProvider`. Notifications stack, carry a title and a body, and suit events that happened elsewhere (a finished export, a new comment) rather than the result of the user's last action.
- **useSnackbar** — `import { useSnackbar } from "wimui/feedback"` — Show a single message bar at the edge of the screen from anywhere under `SnackbarProvider`. One message at a time: showing a new one replaces the current one. Use it when the message may carry one action (for example "Undo").
- **useTableSort** — `import { useTableSort } from "wimui/data-display"` — Sort rows on the client for `Table`: clicking the same column cycles ascending → descending → unsorted. For server-side sorting, keep the state yourself and pass `onSortChange`.
- **useToast** — `import { useToast } from "wimui/feedback"` — Show a short, self-dismissing message (a toast) from anywhere under `ToastProvider`. Use it for a one-off confirmation of something the user just did; for state that stays true (a limit, an outage), render an inline `Alert` instead.
- **useWim** — `import { useWim } from "wimui"` — Read the nearest `WimProvider` values, or fall back to document / i18n globals when used outside a provider.

## Not a component — compose it from existing ones

These names exist in other systems' vocabularies. wimui does not ship them as components because existing components already express them; build them from the components named here instead of hand-rolling new markup.

- **Radio Card** (aka Checkbox Card, Radio Card Group, Tile Group, Radio Tile, Selectable Tile, Select Box Group) — A card-shaped choice. Put a `Radio` (one choice) or `Checkbox` (several) with its label and description inside a `Card`, and group them with `RadioGroup` / `CheckboxGroup` so the keyboard and form value stay native.
- **Native Select** — Use a plain `<select>` element; when it must match WIM styling and behaviour, use `Select`.
- **Toggle Button** — A single press-and-stay button (`aria-pressed`): a `ToggleGroup` with `selectionMode="multiple"` and one option. For an on/off setting, use `Switch`.
- **Collapsible** — A single show/hide section: an `Accordion` with one item and `collapsible`.
- **Navigation Menu** (aka Mega Menu, Megamenu) — Site-level navigation with dropdown panels: a row of `Dropdown`s whose items are links, inside `Navbar` or `Header`.
- **Navigation Progress** (aka NProgress, Top Loading Bar, Page Progress Bar) — A thin bar at the top of the page while a route loads: a `Progress` (use `indeterminate` when the duration is unknown) kept at the top edge with `Affix` (`offsetTop={0}`).
- **Timezone Select** (aka Time Zone Picker) — A searchable list of time zones: a `Combobox` whose `options` come from `Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")`.
- **Swap** — Swapping one icon for another (open/close chevron, play/pause): render the two `Icon`s conditionally and animate the change with `Transition`. Keep the accessible name on the button, not the icon.
- **Counter Badge** (aka Notification Badge, Counter Label) — A count such as "99+": pass the text to `Badge`'s `content`. To pin it to the corner of another element, use `Indicator`.
- **Compound Button** — A button with a second line of description: put two lines of text inside `Button` (a short label first, the description in `Text` below it).
- **Inline Drawer** — A side panel that pushes the content aside instead of overlaying it: a `Splitter` (resizable) or a `Flex` row whose side pane is shown with `Transition`.
- **Expandable Search** — A search icon that opens into a field: an `IconButton` that reveals a `SearchInput` and moves focus into it.
- **Tearsheet** — A large task surface over the page: a `Dialog` or a `Drawer` holding the task. Neither has an extra-wide preset, so set the content width with your own class.
- **Notifications Panel** — A panel listing recent notifications: a `List` inside a `Popover` (from a bell `IconButton`) or a `Drawer`.
- **Guide Banner** (aka Interstitial Screen) — Onboarding guidance: a dismissible `Banner` in the page, or a `Dialog` containing a `Carousel` of steps for a first-run screen. For pointing at parts of the UI, use `Tour`.
- **Options Tile** — A tile that expands to reveal settings: an `Accordion` item styled with the `Card` surface.
- **Add Select** — Picking items from a catalogue to add: a `Dialog` containing `Transfer` (two lists) or `MultiSelect`.
- **Chat Button** (aka AI Skeleton) — AI-styled controls and loading placeholders: a regular `Button` or `Skeleton` marked with `AILabel`. WIM does not give AI content a separate visual style.
- **Shape Indicator** — A status shown by shape as well as colour: an `Icon` whose shape differs per status, followed by the status text.
- **Status Dot** (aka Status Light) — A coloured dot before a status label: an `Indicator` with `inline`, followed by the status text. Never rely on the colour alone. For a person's availability, use `Presence`.
- **Multistep Dialog** (aka Wizard Dialog) — A dialog that walks through steps: a `Dialog` with a `Stepper` at the top and the current step's content below.
- **Compound Tag** — A two-part "key: value" tag: put the key and the value as two pieces of text inside one `Tag`.
- **Entity Title** — An icon, title and subtitle as one unit: `Group` with an `Icon`, a `Title` and a `Text`. For a person, use `Persona`.
- **Index Filters** (aka Filter Bar, Data Filters) — A filter bar above a table: a `SearchInput` plus `Select` / `MultiSelect` controls, with the active filters shown as removable `Chip`s (`onDelete`).
- **Contextual Save Bar** — A bar announcing unsaved changes with Save and Discard: a `Banner` (or content kept in view with `Affix`) holding two `Button`s.
- **Data View** — Switching a collection between list and grid: a `SegmentedControl` that swaps between `List` and `SimpleGrid`.
- **Callout Card** — A promotional card with an illustration and a call to action: a `Card` with an `Image` and a `Button`.
- **Slider Input** — A slider with a number field beside it: a `Slider` and a `NumberInput` bound to the same value.

## Not in scope — deliberately not provided

These exist in other systems' vocabularies and are **decisions, not gaps**. Do not hand-roll them into a wimui screen; the alternative given is the supported way to express the same intent.

- **Parallax Scrolling** (aka Parallax, Scroll Parallax, Parallax Hero, Parallax Hero Images, Parallax Scroll, Hero Parallax, Sticky Scroll Reveal, Macbook Scroll, Container Scroll Animation) — Backgrounds moving at a different speed from the foreground. The motion does not correspond to any change of state, which is what this system animates. If the goal is to show scroll position, show the position. Use `ScrollProgress` instead.
- **Text Scramble** (aka Scramble Text, Decrypt Text, Glitch Text, Hyper Text, Encrypted Text) — Randomising characters before settling on the real string. The reader parses the same sentence twice and gets nothing for the lost legibility. The one case where text legitimately arrives character by character is model output, which StreamingText already covers. Use `StreamingText` instead.
- **Spring Animation** (aka Spring Physics, Springs, Physics-based Animation) — A physics engine (mass / stiffness / damping props solved in a rAF loop). The bounce curve itself already exists as the `--wim-easing-spring` token, which is what press and swipe-return use. Adding the engine would put physics parameters into the public contract and move motion from CSS to JS. Use `--wim-easing-spring` instead.
- **Choropleth Map** (aka Choropleth, Filled Map, Region Map, Geo Map, World Map) — A map shading regions by value. Shipping boundary data would put its size and a political stance on disputed borders into a UI library, and large regions dominate regardless of their values. Regions are compared more accurately in a sorted bar chart. Use `BarChart` instead.
- **Animated Text Effects** (aka Animated Gradient Text, Animated Shiny Text, Aurora Text, Morphing Text, Sparkles Text, Spinning Text, Text Reveal, Typing Animation, Word Rotate, Line Shadow Text, Comic Text, Kinetic Text, Video Text, Text 3D Flip, Text Animate, Dia Text Reveal, Canvas Text, Layout Text Flip, Colourful Text, Squiggly Text, Text Generate Effect, Typewriter Effect, Flip Words, Text Hover Effect, Container Text Flip, Hero Highlight, Text Reveal Card, Text Flipping Board, Text Rotate, Pointer Highlight, Container Cover) — Text that shimmers, rotates, morphs or types itself out. It cannot be read while it moves, and keeps moving after it has been read. Emphasis is a matter of weight, colour and size; the one case where text legitimately arrives piece by piece is model output, which StreamingText covers. Use `Text` instead.
- **Decorative Background Pattern** (aka Dot Pattern, Grid Pattern, Animated Grid Pattern, Interactive Grid Pattern, Flickering Grid, Hexagon Pattern, Striped Pattern, Retro Grid, Noise Texture, Dither Field, Light Rays, Meteors, Particles, Warp Background, Glyph Matrix, Backlight, Floating 3D Particles, Ripple, Dotted Glow Background, Background Ripple Effect, Sparkles, Background Gradient, Gradient Animation, Wavy Background, Background Boxes, Background Beams, Background Beams With Collision, Background Lines, Aurora Background, Glowing Stars, Shooting Stars, Vortex, Background Cubes Grid, Cloud Shader, Grid and Dot Backgrounds, Noise Background, Dither Shader, Webcam Pixel Grid, Matrix Trail, Lamp Effect, Scales) — Patterns and particles laid behind content that carry no meaning of their own. They make the background under text uneven, which costs contrast, and moving ones compete with real motion in the foreground. Separate surfaces with the surface tokens and borders instead. Use `Box` instead.
- **Animated Button Effects** (aka Shimmer Button, Shiny Button, Rainbow Button, Pulsating Button, Ripple Button, Interactive Hover Button, Animated Subscribe Button, Confetti, Cool Mode, Magnetic Button, Stateful Button, Pixel Prompt Button, Paper Plane Send) — Buttons that shimmer, pulse, ripple or burst into confetti. They only attract attention before the click, and once several buttons do it the primary action is lost. Rank actions with Button variants, and report the result through the state change and an announcement. Use `Button` instead.
- **Glow and Spotlight Card** (aka Magic Card, Neon Gradient Card, Shine Border, Glare Hover, Lens, Progressive Blur, Blur Fade, Pixel Image, 3D Card Effect, Evervault Card, Card Hover Effect, Wobble Card, Card Spotlight, Focus Cards, Comet Card, Glare Card, Direction Aware Hover, Glowing Effect, Hover Border Gradient, Moving Border, Liquid Glass, Chromatic Image, Canvas Reveal Effect, SVG Mask Effect, Hover 3D, Aura) — Cards with glowing borders, a spotlight that follows the pointer, or content that fades in from a blur. Nothing happens for touch or keyboard users, and for pointer users it does not help tell the cards apart. Use Card variants and the heading inside the card. Use `Card` instead.
- **Device Mockup** (aka iPhone Mockup, Android Mockup, Safari Mockup, Browser Frame, Device Frame, Mockup) — Phone and browser frames around a screenshot. It is marketing artwork rather than an interface component, and the frames go out of date with every device generation. Show the screenshot with Image, with the frame baked into the image if one is needed. Use `Image` instead.
- **Decorative Motion Graphics** (aka Globe, Icon Cloud, Orbiting Circles, Animated Beam, Dock, Scroll Based Velocity, Animated List, Dotted Map, Smooth Cursor, Pointer Effect, Hero Video Dialog, GitHub Globe, 3D Globe, Paper Plane Globe, Floating Dock, Following Pointer, 3D Pin, 3D Marquee, Gravity Trail, Image Particles, Image Wave, Disintegrating Gallery, ASCII Art, Pixelated Canvas, SVG Path Morphing, Google Gemini Effect, Tracing Beam, Images Badge, Direction Aware Selection, Card Stack, Draggable Card, Infinite Card Grid, Grid Zoom Image, Hover Image Links, Hover Gallery, Image Generation Loader, Notch, Fluid Notch) — Spinning globes, floating icon clouds, beams between logos, a magnifying dock, a custom cursor: motion that carries no information. It pulls attention away from the content and is a burden for people who reduce motion. Show relationships with NodeGraph, items with List, and a video with Video inside a Dialog. Use `List` instead.
- **Social Post Embed** (aka Tweet Card, Client Tweet Card, Tweet Embed) — Embedding a post from a social network in that network's own look. Its appearance and the way it is fetched change on the provider's schedule, which a design system cannot keep up with. Quote it in a Blockquote or Card with a link to the source. Use `Card` instead.
- **Animated Input Effects** (aka Placeholders And Vanish Input, Gooey Input, Gooey Waitlist) — Input fields whose placeholder cycles through phrases, whose text dissolves on submit, or whose outline stretches like goo. A moving placeholder changes before it can be read and is no substitute for a label. Report the result of a submission through the field's state and an announcement. Use `Input` instead.

---
For per-component props, types and defaults, see `llms-full.txt`.

**One component, matching your installed version:** the package ships `dist/llms/<Component>.md` — every prop with its type and default, its sub-components, and the design tokens it reads (e.g. `node_modules/wimui/dist/llms/Select.md`, also exported as `wimui/llms/Select.md`). The hosted copy of this file tracks main and can be ahead of the release you installed.
